text:
Emma (Sales): quick heads-up — AcmeCorp wants a 2-week POC. They need us to provide a stable outbound IP footprint for their firewall team. They asked about rotating IPs during the POC and whether we can offer a customer-side proxy option.

Raj (Solutions Eng): we can do 2 options: 1) reserve static SNAT IP(s) from our Dedicated pool; 2) provide guidance for routing through a customer-managed proxy/bastion. which do they prefer? @Emma

Emma (Sales): customer prefers minimal infra changes, so they want a fixed set of IPs they can whitelist. but security also asked about short-lived creds in case keys leak.

Sofia (Net Eng): we can assign up to 4 static outbound IPs for a POC Dedicated endpoint. they appear as our SNAT on egress. rotation is possible but not recommended mid-POC unless we give them the new list in advance.

Sofia (Net Eng): sample firewall rule we usually share with customers:```Allow TCP 443 from 34.198.200.123/32, 34.198.200.124/32```

Raj (Solutions Eng): if they want rotation, propose a weekly rotation window and a 48h change notification. otherwise stick to static for the 2 weeks. also note IPs might map to different AZs — traffic stays global.

Oliver (SE): pricing Q — for a 2-week Dedicated POC (single small GPU pool) do we give a waived setup or prorated reserved capacity? need a number to put in the SOW.

Raj (Solutions Eng): for short POCs we usually offer a time-boxed discounted rate: 50% of monthly reserved price, billed pro-rata for duration. I'll confirm with finance.

Maria (Security): we need to document audit controls. ask Acme for: expected client IPs, contact for firewall changes, and their data retention constraints. also recommend ephemeral API keys scoped to the POC project and rotation every 7 days. :lock:

Emma (Sales): @Maria — they filled a 3rd-party security questionnaire earlier; i'll attach it to the ticket. they are SOC2-aware but want logs of outbound NAT mappings. can we provide per-request IP logging?

Sofia (Net Eng): we capture egress SNAT mappings in flow logs for Dedicated; we can export a CSV with timestamp + src/dst + SNAT IP for the POC window. that'll satisfy most security teams.

Oliver (SE): small implementation note for their infra team — if they can't allow our IPs, we can offer a proxy pattern: they run a forward proxy in their VPC and route requests through it. we'll provide example config:```# curl via company proxy
curl -x http://proxy.company.internal:3128 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate```

Emma (Sales): should I ask them whether they prefer the proxy or static IP list? I'll also get their expected QPS so we can size the pool.

Raj (Solutions Eng): yes — ask QPS and whether traffic is bursty. also ask if they need mTLS between their proxy and our endpoint.

Maria (Security): add: for keys, use scoped POC API keys limited to models + rate limits. log access and produce a short audit summary at end of POC.

deploy-bot: created ticket <https://tickets.internal/POC-2985|POC-2985> for network allowlist + audit export :white_check_mark:

Emma (Sales): next steps for me: 1) ask Acme for proxy vs static IP preference, 2) request client firewall contact + expected QPS, 3) attach their filled questionnaire to ticket. I'll ping back with answers. :thumbsup:

Raj (Solutions Eng): I'll follow up with finance on pricing and confirm the 2-week discounted prorate.

Sofia (Net Eng): once they commit, we need a quick network change window to allocate SNATs and confirm flow-log export path. expect ~4 business hours.

Maria (Security): I'll draft the minimal security checklist for the SOW (keys, logs, rotation cadence).

Emma (Sales): thanks everyone — looping in Acme now.

Acme Firewall Admin (external): thx — prefer static IPs, expected peak ~120 RPS, no mTLS for now. please send whitelist list and duration.

Emma (Sales): noted. leaving this open for the handoff.
